flags: CRITERIA / DROP CANDIDATE (lot allowance): area page 'Things to Do When You Visit': 'Camping: Open Camping-Walk/Float/Backpack(no Deer/Turkey); Designated Camping Sites'. The area map (Conservation Commission © 08/17) legend is Boundary, Paved Road, Gravel Road, Drainage, Parking Lot, Privy, Boat Ramp, Forest, Topography - no camping symbol anywhere; it draws one lot with a privy and boat ramp at the end of the gravel road on the north shore and a second lot on Route RA at the east boundary. MDC's GIS camping layer (27) has no point for the area; the parking layer (26) has lot 1308 (the ramp lot, 'Paved', Allows_Trailers 'No') and lot 1309 (40.34011,-92.00527, the RA lot, 'Paved', Allows_Trailers 'No'). The page's regulations: 'Vehicle use is restricted to graveled and paved roads and established parking areas'. So a vehicle camper can only be in the ramp lot (~35 x 40 m gravel, ramp off its south corner, privy at its SE edge) or the small roadside lot on RA; the 'Open Camping' listing is walk/float/backpack. That is the ramp-lot pattern the brief drops (Cross Timbers, Dodd Access, Bird's Blue Hole).

WATERFRONT (lakefront -> lakeview, if kept): there is no camping spot to measure from. On the 0.38 m/px frame the ramp lot's west edge is ~10-15 m from the lake across a grassy, brushy bank and the ramp runs into the water off its south corner; the lake is plainly in view from the lot. The lot is itself the boat-ramp lot, which the on-water rule excludes, so lakefront fails; lakeview holds. The lake is roughly 4 ha (~10 acres) on imagery, over the 5-acre pond line. The Route RA lot is ~60 m from the lake's east arm through trees and a road embankment (not waterfront).
PIN: stored 40.34232,-92.00798 = GIS lot 1308, the ramp lot. Fine for what is there.
